name: selfblog
help: Blog system for selfdoc-based documentation sites

check.name: check
check.help: Check blog posts and unified multi-project documentation. For unified docs-site projects, runs the full documentation check across every constituent project plus the docs-site's own content; otherwise validates blog posts (POST001-POST005).

flags.name: ignore
flags.help: Comma-separated lint codes to suppress (e.g., SEO007,SEO008)

flags.name: auto-commit
flags.help: Automatically commit updated content hash tracking files to git after checking

build.name: build
build.help: Build blog posts, the unified documentation site, or the home project

flags.name: target
flags.help: Build target: 'posts' for posts-only build, 'unified' for unified multi-project site, 'home' for the assembly's home project (the one served at the site root, whose pages carry site-level directives)

flags.name: drafts
flags.help: Include posts marked as draft in the build output

flags.name: auto-commit
flags.help: Automatically commit updated content hash tracking files to git after the build

flags.name: site-manifests
flags.help: Path to the assembly's manifests directory. Required by --target home: the home project's front page renders the curated listing with each project's live version and the recent posts across the whole site, and only the assembly's manifests carry those.

flags.name: docs-base
flags.help: Base URL of the assembled site, for the absolute links the site-level directives emit. Required by --target home.

post.name: post
post.help: Manage blog posts and chronological content for the documentation site

new.name: new
new.help: Scaffold a new blog post markdown file with a date-prefixed filename and frontmatter template containing title, date, slug, tags, draft status, and project metadata. Creates the file in the configured posts directory and exits with an error if the file already exists.

flags.name: title
flags.help: Title for the new blog post, used in frontmatter and filename generation

list.name: list
list.help: List all discovered blog posts with date, title, slug, and draft status. Scans the configured posts directory for markdown files with frontmatter, parses their metadata, and prints a formatted summary showing each post's publication date, title, slug identifier, and whether it is marked as a draft.

generate.name: generate
generate.help: Generate a blog post markdown file from structured release metadata. Takes version, bump type, description, changelog, and registry URLs as inputs, produces a frontmatter-bearing post with title, date, tags, and body content, and updates the project manifest with the new post entry.

flags.name: from-release
flags.help: Generate the post from structured release metadata rather than freeform content

flags.name: version
flags.help: The released version number to feature in the generated blog post title and metadata

flags.name: prev-version
flags.help: Previous version number, used to show what version this release upgrades from

flags.name: bump-type
flags.help: Semver bump type (patch, minor, or major) included in the post frontmatter

flags.name: description
flags.help: Short release description text included as the post summary paragraph

flags.name: context
flags.help: Additional context explaining the rationale for this release, included in generated blog posts

flags.name: changelog-file
flags.help: Path to a markdown file whose contents are embedded as the changelog section of the post

flags.name: body-file
flags.help: Path to a file containing user-written prose to include as the main post body content

flags.name: project-name
flags.help: Human-readable project name used in the blog post title and frontmatter metadata

flags.name: release-url
flags.help: Full URL to the GitHub release page, linked from the generated blog post

flags.name: registry-url
flags.help: Package registry URL such as PyPI or npm page, can be specified multiple times

publish.name: publish
publish.help: Publish non-draft blog posts to the documentation assembly. Builds posts locally, pushes built HTML and manifest to the assembly repo via the Git Data API, then dispatches a shared-only workflow to regenerate cross-project elements.

grants.name: assembly-dispatch
grants.reason: triggers a GitHub Actions workflow on the assembly repository, which rebuilds and republishes the live documentation site

docs.name: docs
docs.help: Publish this project's documentation to the unified assembly without a release

publish.name: publish
publish.help: Publish this project's documentation to the assembly without a release. Builds the docs locally, pushes the built site, its manifest and its membership record into the assembly repo via the Git Data API -- deleting the pages this project published before and no longer produces -- then dispatches a shared-only workflow to regenerate cross-project elements.

grants.name: assembly-dispatch
grants.reason: triggers a GitHub Actions workflow on the assembly repository, which rebuilds and republishes the live documentation site

assembly.name: assembly
assembly.help: Manage the unified multi-project documentation assembly and deployment

init.name: init
init.help: Create and initialize the assembly GitHub repository with workflow and configuration files. Creates a private GitHub repo, pushes initial files via the Contents API, creates a Cloudflare Pages project if credentials are available, and sets GitHub secrets for deployment authentication.

grants.name: create-repo
grants.reason: creates a new private GitHub repository under the configured owner; repository creation is not undone by rerunning the command

grants.name: create-pages-project
grants.reason: creates a Cloudflare Pages project on the configured account, claiming its *.pages.dev subdomain

grants.name: set-secret
grants.reason: writes Cloudflare deployment credentials into the assembly repository's GitHub Actions secrets

push.name: push
push.help: Dispatch a GitHub Actions workflow to rebuild this project in the documentation assembly. Detects the source repository, resolves the latest git tag as the version reference, and sends a repository dispatch event to the assembly repo with the project slug, version, and commit SHA.

grants.name: assembly-dispatch
grants.reason: triggers a GitHub Actions workflow on the assembly repository, which rebuilds and republishes the live documentation site

status.name: status
status.help: Show the status of recent assembly build workflow runs on GitHub. Queries the assembly repository for recent workflow runs using the GitHub CLI and displays their status, conclusion, and timing information for monitoring deployment progress.

rebuild.name: rebuild
rebuild.help: Dispatch rebuild workflows for every project registered in the assembly. Fetches the projects.json manifest from the assembly repository, then sends a separate GitHub Actions repository dispatch event for each registered project to trigger a full documentation rebuild.

grants.name: assembly-dispatch
grants.reason: triggers a GitHub Actions workflow on the assembly repository, which rebuilds and republishes the live documentation site

retire.name: retire
retire.help: Retire a project from the unified assembly: remove its [[project]] block from the roster and, in the same commit, delete its whole site subtree, all of its manifests and its membership record, then dispatch a shared-only rebuild so the listing, feed, sitemap and search index stop naming it.

flags.name: slug
flags.help: Slug of the project to retire; it is removed from the roster and every path it owns in the assembly is deleted

grants.name: assembly-commit
grants.reason: deletes a project's published documentation from the assembly repository's deploy branch through the GitHub Git Data API

grants.name: assembly-dispatch
grants.reason: triggers a GitHub Actions workflow on the assembly repository, which rebuilds and republishes the live documentation site

redirects.name: redirects
redirects.help: Generate a Cloudflare Pages _redirects file for this project that redirects standalone documentation URLs to the corresponding paths on the unified assembly site. Requires a project slug and assembly base URL as inputs, prints the redirect rules to stdout.

flags.name: slug
flags.help: Project slug used as the URL path segment in the assembly site structure

flags.name: docs-base
flags.help: Base URL of the assembly documentation site used for generating redirect targets

generate-shared.name: generate-shared
generate-shared.help: Generate the shared cross-project elements for the assembled documentation site. Reads per-project manifest JSON files, merges post overlays, and produces a homepage, blog index, navigation JSON, RSS feed, XML sitemap, robots.txt, a site-wide llms.txt linking to each project's own, a root 404 page, a security headers file and the redirect worker in the site output directory.

flags.name: site-dir
flags.help: Path to the combined site output directory where shared HTML files are written

flags.name: manifests-dir
flags.help: Path to the directory containing per-project manifest JSON files for the assembly

flags.name: docs-base
flags.help: Base URL used for in-page links in the generated feed, listing and blog index. May be root-relative or empty. The sitemap does not read it: every <loc> is absolute by protocol, so the sitemap is generated from --canonical-base whatever this says.

flags.name: canonical-base
flags.help: Absolute canonical base URL of the assembly site, from topology.docs_base (e.g. 'https://docs.smmh.dev'). Required: it is the one hostname that serves content and every other host 301s onto it, it is the base of every sitemap entry, and it targets the rel=canonical links on the homepage and blog index, so it cannot be root-relative like --docs-base.

flags.name: legacy-blog-host
flags.help: Hostname of a retired blog subdomain (e.g. 'blog.smmh.dev') to 301 onto the canonical blog URL. Empty when no such subdomain exists.

flags.name: home-slug
flags.help: The roster's home project: the one project served at the site root. Its pages are left out of the generated listing and out of nav, and every site-level directive region it emitted is re-rendered from the current manifests. Empty means the tree carries no home project (which the deploy path never does -- the roster requires one).

integrate.name: integrate
integrate.help: Integrate one dispatched project into the assembly repository checkout and push the result. Builds the cloned source project, replaces its subtree under site/, refreshes its manifest and membership record, regenerates the shared cross-project elements, rebuilds the search index, then commits and pushes with a re-sync retry loop so concurrent deploys converge instead of clobbering each other. This is the whole body of the generated deploy workflow.

flags.name: slug
flags.help: Project slug being integrated; the site subtree is site/<slug>/. Required unless --scope is 'shared-only'.

flags.name: version
flags.help: Version of the project being integrated, recorded in projects.json and the commit message

flags.name: ref
flags.help: Git ref (tag) the source project was cloned at, recorded in projects.json

flags.name: source-repo
flags.help: Source project repository (owner/name), recorded in projects.json

flags.name: scope
flags.help: What this dispatch replaces: 'full' (the whole project subtree plus this project's posts), 'posts' (only this project's posts, at the site-level site/blog/<post-slug>/), or 'shared-only' (no project files, just the cross-project elements). Empty means 'full'.

flags.name: canonical-base
flags.help: Absolute canonical base URL of the assembly site, from topology.docs_base. Required: it targets the redirect worker and the rel=canonical links.

flags.name: legacy-blog-host
flags.help: Hostname of a retired blog subdomain to 301 onto the canonical blog URL. Empty when no such subdomain exists.

flags.name: assembly-dir
flags.help: Path to the assembly repository checkout being updated

flags.name: source-dir
flags.help: Path to the cloned source project. Defaults to <assembly-dir>/source/<slug>, where the deploy workflow clones it.

flags.name: branch
flags.help: Assembly repository branch the deploy commits and pushes to

flags.name: attempts
flags.help: How many times to re-sync with the remote and retry the push before failing

grants.name: assembly-commit
grants.reason: pushes a commit to the assembly repository's deploy branch, which is the content the live documentation site serves

verify.name: verify
verify.help: Assert every property a built assembly tree has to have before it is deployed: that the roster, the site subtrees and the manifests name the same projects, that each manifest's pages and posts were actually emitted, that the shared cross-project artifacts exist and parse, that every internal reference, sitemap entry, feed link and cross-project link resolves, that every page has a title and a canonical, and that no unresolved directive or per-project routing file survived. The deploy runs this itself before it pushes; this command is how you run the same assertions by hand against a checkout.

flags.name: assembly-dir
flags.help: Path to the assembly repository checkout to verify

flags.name: canonical-base
flags.help: Absolute canonical base URL of the assembly site, from topology.docs_base. Required: it is what tells this site's absolute URLs from everybody else's, and without it half the assertions would pass by not looking.

sync-workflow.name: sync-workflow
sync-workflow.help: Regenerate the assembly repository's deploy workflow from this project's configuration and push it. The deployed workflow is a generated artifact like any other: without this it stays frozen at whatever the template said when 'assembly init' ran. Pushes only when the content actually differs.

flags.name: pin-version
flags.help: selfblog version the regenerated workflow pins its toolchain install to. Defaults to the running selfblog's version, which is what the release path wants: the workflow names the selfblog that generated it.

flags.name: pin-selfdoc
flags.help: selfdoc version the regenerated workflow pins its toolchain install to. Defaults to the selfdoc installed in this environment; selfdoc missing here is a hard error, never an unpinned install.

flags.name: pin-pagefind
flags.help: pagefind version the regenerated workflow pins its toolchain install to. Defaults to PyPI's current release: pagefind is a CI-only tool nothing here installs, so there is no local version to read.

grants.name: assembly-commit
grants.reason: commits the regenerated deploy workflow to the assembly repository through the GitHub Git Data API
